title: Sum of distances in a tree
statement: For every node of a tree with n nodes, return the sum of its distances to all other nodes.
hints: One DFS from the root computes subtree sizes and the answer for the root.
Moving the root from parent p to child c: the size[c] nodes in c's subtree get 1 closer, the other n − size[c] get 1 farther.

solution.explanation: Rerooting: compute everything for one root bottom-up, then push answers top-down with an O(1) adjustment per edge: ans[c] = ans[p] − size[c] + (n − size[c]). Running a BFS from every node would be O(n²). Iterative traversal avoids Python's recursion limit on the path-shaped test.
